samples.summary: Merge budget is enforced only in client-side code on the CRDT path; the server never validates worksheet content, so any actor with document write access (including an anonymous share-link `editor`) can persist an unbounded merge map and permanently DoS the document for every collaborator.
samples.evidence: The change adds `mergeBudgetAdmits` to `YorkieStore.applyMerge` and documents it as "the floor under a path that reaches the CRDT directly", but that floor runs in the browser bundle. The only server-side gate on Yorkie traffic is `YorkieAuthController` (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts), which authorizes *who* may write (`hasAccess` -> membership or `link.role === 'editor'`) and never inspects the change pack contents; I found no backend validator of `ws.merges` on the push path (only `parseMerges`, reachable solely from `PUT /api/v1/.../merges`). Attack: a share-link editor mints a Yorkie token at `GET /auth/yorkie-token` (the public key ships in every visitor's bundle, per that controller's own comment), attaches with a hand-rolled client, and writes `merges` with ~10^6 anchors or a single `{rs: 1e6, cs: 18278}` span. Every later load runs `Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap` (sheet.ts:861), one Map entry per covered cell — the document becomes unopenable for all collaborators, exactly the failure `MaxMergedCells` exists to prevent, with no UI left to undo it. The new backend walks (`snapFreezePastMerges`, `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze`) then run over that attacker-sized map synchronously inside `doc.update`.

samples.summary: A single non-finite (`NaN`) span silently disables the entire merge budget for a worksheet — every comparison against `NaN` is false, so `mergeBudgetAdmits` admits everything afterwards.
samples.evidence: `mergeBudgetOf` (merging.ts:58) sums `span.rs * span.cs` with no finiteness check, and `mergeBudgetAdmits` gates on `cells > MaxMergedCells` (line 95) and `budget.coveredCells > MaxMergeCoveredCells` (line 72). With one stored span of `rs: NaN`, `coveredCells` becomes `NaN`, `NaN > MaxMergeCoveredCells` is false, and `mergeBudgetError` returns `null` — the cap is off for every writer that derives its budget from the stored map: `Sheet.canMergeSelection` (via `this.mergeBudget` from `rebuildMergeCoverMap`), `YorkieStore.applyMerge`, and `applyMergeRanges` in the XLSX importer. `NaN`/`Infinity` cannot come from `parseMerges` (assertInt) but is trivially writable on the unvalidated CRDT path (see the client-side-enforcement finding), so one poisoned entry turns off the DoS guard this whole change is built on; `Infinity` additionally makes `rebuildMergeCoverMap`'s `for (let r = anchor.r; r < anchor.r + span.rs; r++)` loop forever.

samples.summary: `YorkieStore.applyMerge` skips the budget check entirely when the anchor already exists, so replacing an existing merge with an arbitrarily large span is unbounded on the very path the change calls the CRDT floor.
samples.evidence: The guard is `if (!ws.merges[sref] && !mergeBudgetAdmits(...)) return;` — the short-circuit means any `setMerge` whose `sref` is already a key is written with no cap at all (`ws.merges[sref] = { ...span }`, line 993). `Sheet.applyPasteMerges` and `moveRangeTo` both call `store.setMerge` with computed anchors that can coincide with a surviving anchor, and anything driving the store directly can issue `setMerge(A1, {rs: 1000000, cs: 18278})` once any `A1` merge exists. The stated purpose — keeping the map inside what the load-time `rebuildMergeCoverMap` walk can afford — is defeated by a per-anchor replacement, whose cell count is never compared against `MaxMergedCells`.

samples.summary: `PUT .../freeze` now calls `parseRef` on *stored* merge keys with no try/catch, so one unparseable key (which nothing validates on the CRDT path) turns the endpoint into a permanent 500 for that tab.
samples.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges(safeWorksheetRecordEntries(ws.merges ?? {}), rows, cols)` reaches `ranges.push(toMergeRange(parseRef(anchorSref), span))` (merging.ts:321), and `parseRef` throws a bare `Error('Invalid Reference')` for any key without a digit (coordinates.ts:350-352). Merge keys are round-trip validated only on `PUT merges`; a collaborator writing the CRDT directly — or a legacy/migrated document, cf. `cloneMergeRecord` in worksheet-shape-migration.ts:86, which copies legacy keys verbatim — can seat a key like `"ZZ"` or `""`. The throw lands inside `doc.update`, rolling the update back and surfacing as an unhandled 500, so a low-privileged writer permanently denies the freeze endpoint for that tab on an otherwise valid request. Before this change `PUT freeze` never read `ws.merges` at all. I could not confirm a non-CRDT injection route for a bad key, hence low confidence.

samples.summary: Server-side CPU amplification: the new freeze snap copies and sorts the whole stored merge array twice per call, synchronously inside `doc.update`, on every v1 insert/delete/freeze — over state with no server-enforced ceiling.
samples.evidence: `sweep` does `[...ranges].sort(...)` and is called once per axis, so each `snapFreezePastMerges` allocates three arrays of the merge count and performs two O(n log n) sorts. It now runs in `shiftWorksheetViewState` (worksheet-structure.ts, every `POST insert` / `POST delete`) and in `PUT freeze` (worksheet.controller.ts:121), both on the backend's single Node event loop inside a synchronous `doc.update`. `MaxMergeEntries` bounds only what `PUT merges` accepts; a map grown through the unvalidated CRDT path or a legacy document is unbounded, so an attacker who first seats a large map can loop cheap `POST insert` calls to stall the event loop for all tenants. The pre-existing `shiftMergeMap` walk was O(n) with no sort or array copies, so this is an amplification of an existing walk rather than a new class of exposure.

samples.summary: Validate-then-mutate on `PUT freeze`: the grid bound `parseFreeze` enforces to prevent an unrecoverable render DoS is applied to the request value but not to the snapped value actually stored.
samples.evidence: `parseFreeze` bounds `rows`/`cols` to `MaxRows`/`MaxColumns` and its comment says why: "an out-of-grid freeze allocates per frame and the UI never paints — which also means the user cannot reach the freeze menu to undo it" (worksheet-settings.ts:50-57). Line 126 writes the *snapped* value — the far edge of a straddling merge — which is never re-checked against those bounds. Merge extents are grid-bounded only on the `PUT merges` path (`rs <= MaxRows - anchor.r + 1`); the XLSX importer (`applyMergeRanges`, xlsx-importer.ts:262, which computes spans from arbitrary file-supplied refs via `safeParseRef`) and the CRDT path apply no grid bound at all, so a merge ending past row 1,000,000 lets a benign-looking `{rows: 1}` request persist an out-of-grid freeze — the state the validator exists to refuse. The same unbounded write happens in `shiftWorksheetViewState` on insert/delete; clamping the snapped result to the grid before storing closes it.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. The merge budget is enforced only in browser code (yorkie-store.ts:987-993, whose own comment calls it "the floor under a path that reaches the CRDT directly"). The only server-side budget enforcement, parseMerges (backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:127,163,178), is reachable solely from the REST body handler worksheet.controller.ts:243; worksheet-structure.controller.ts only reads/shifts existing merges. The two Yorkie webhooks are the sole server touchpoints on CRDT traffic: yorkie-auth.controller.ts authorizes identity+verb only (its body type has no content field, lines 19-27; checkAttribute/hasAccess lines 319-374), and yorkie-event.controller.ts only mirrors updatedAt, its comment stating content edits "flow client to Yorkie only, never through this backend". A repo-wide grep for PushPull/changePack found no backend change-pack inspection at all, and docker-compose runs stock yorkie with no limits. No compensating read-path clamp exists either: getMerges (yorkie-store.ts:1037-1045) copies entries unfiltered via safeWorksheetRecordEntries (worksheet-record.ts:47-61, which only handles duplicate-key TypeErrors), feeding Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap (sheet.ts:862-877), which allocates one Map entry per covered cell with no ceiling. So an anonymous share-link editor — exactly the low-trust actor docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:245-257 says client-side mounts do not bound — can mint a token, attach with a non-browser client, and persist a merge map that makes the document unopenable for all collaborators. In-lane as unsafe handling of attacker-controlled input where the only enforcement sits on the client side of a trust boundary; major impact.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists exactly as described. merging.ts:53-61 sums span.rs*span.cs with no finiteness check; merging.ts:95 (`cells > MaxMergedCells`) and merging.ts:69-74 (`entries > MaxMergeEntries`, `coveredCells > MaxMergeCoveredCells`) are all strict `>` comparisons that evaluate false for NaN, so mergeBudgetError returns null and mergeBudgetAdmits admits unconditionally once any NaN span is in the stored budget. All three named consumers derive their budget from the stored map without sanitizing it: sheet.ts:862-877/4883 (rebuildMergeCoverMap -> this.mergeBudget -> canMergeSelection), yorkie-store.ts:987-993 (applyMerge recomputes from raw CRDT `ws.merges` and writes `{...span}` unvalidated), and xlsx-importer.ts:250 (seeds budget from worksheet.merges). No guard makes it unreachable: a grep for isFinite/Number.isInteger across packages/sheets/src finds no validation of merge spans, and safeWorksheetRecordEntries (worksheet-record.ts:47-61) only handles duplicate-key errors, performing no value checks. The only validator rejecting non-finite spans is parseMerges/assertInt (backend worksheet-settings.ts:155-162), which is on the v1 REST PUT body path only, not on the CRDT write path or any load path. Infinity additionally makes sheet.ts:868's `for (let r = anchor.r; r < anchor.r + span.rs; r++)` non-terminating on load for every collaborator. This is unsanitized untrusted input defeating a resource-exhaustion control, in the security lens's unsafe-input-handling lane, so it is not refutable as not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope.

verdict.reason: The short-circuit is present exactly as quoted (yorkie-store.ts:987-993), but the unbounded-span write it is said to enable is unreachable. Every caller of IStore.setMerge in the repo already enforces the per-span cap before reaching the store: applyPasteMerges guards each span with mergeBudgetAdmits (sheet.ts:2725), which unconditionally rejects cells > MaxMergedCells (merging.ts:95); moveRangeTo re-creates merges with unchanged, already-budgeted spans after deleting them (sheet.ts:2961-2969); mergeSelection is gated by canMergeSelection, which both spends the budget (sheet.ts:4883) and refuses when any merge intersects the selection (sheet.ts:4884) — so the "anchor already exists" branch cannot be hit there. The untrusted-input vectors the reviewer implies are also independently capped upstream: external HTML/TSV pastes carry no merge metadata at all (sheet.ts:2449-2465, pasted merges come only from the internal copyBuffer at sheet.ts:2413-2429), the XLSX importer spends the budget per mergeCell (xlsx-importer.ts:269), and the v1 PUT merges validator rejects rs*cs > MaxMergedCells (worksheet-settings.ts:163,178). The remaining "anything driving the store directly" actor is client-side code that already has unrestricted doc.update access to the same CRDT (the backend validates only the REST path; packages/backend/src/yorkie has no content-validation hook on sync), so the store check is defense-in-depth rather than a security boundary. Under the security rubric this is a hardening gap in an already-guarded resource cap, not an exploitable authz/injection/crypto defect.

verdict.reason: The code exists exactly as quoted (worksheet.controller.ts:121-125 -> merging.ts:320-322 -> coordinates.ts:337-352, and safeWorksheetRecordEntries at worksheet-record.ts:47-61 only recovers duplicate-ownKeys TypeErrors, it does not filter bad keys), so this is not a 'not-present' refutation. It is refuted as out-of-scope for the Security lens: the impact is an unhandled exception -> HTTP 500 (availability/robustness), with no authorization bypass, secret exposure, injection, or broken cryptographic check. The only actor who can seat a malformed merge key is someone who already has CRDT write access to that document and can already destroy its contents through supported endpoints, so there is no privilege escalation or cross-tenant reach. The claimed 'permanent' denial is also wrong: PUT /merges parses only the request body (assertMergesClearOfFreeze is passed the body-derived `merges` at worksheet.controller.ts:253, never ws.merges) and replaces the field wholesale at line 258, so any writer can repair the tab in one call; GET freeze (line 92) and GET merges (line 226) never parse keys. Finally, 'merge keys are valid srefs' is a pre-existing document-wide invariant, not something this endpoint uniquely relies on: worksheet-structure.controller.ts:158 and :195 already call parseRef on stored merge keys, as do worksheet-structure.ts:279/601/694 and sheet.ts:544/1432. A corrupt key breaks the editor and several other endpoints identically, so the freeze endpoint is not a security boundary being weakened. This is a legitimate input-validation/robustness bug for the correctness lens, which the Security rubric explicitly defers ('General logic bugs (correctness lens)').

verdict.reason:
The code is present exactly as quoted — `[...ranges].sort(...)` at merging.ts:331 inside `sweep`, called twice (lines 339, 344), reached from worksheet-structure.ts:278 (`shiftWorksheetViewState`, via `applyWorksheetShift` line 611) and worksheet.controller.ts:121 inside a synchronous `doc.update`. But it is not a blocking security defect under this lens.

(1) No complexity-class change, only a small constant factor. `snapFreezePastMerges` is inherently Theta(n) in the merge count (an exact snap must inspect every merge), and both callers already pay that same Theta(n) with heavier per-element work in the same call. On the insert/delete path, worksheet-structure.ts:598-606 runs `shiftMergeMap(new Map(safeWorksheetRecordEntries(ws.merges)))` immediately before `shiftWorksheetViewState`: it materializes the full entries array (worksheet-record.ts:54), builds a Map, and performs `parseRef` + `toSref` string parse/format per entry (merging.ts:246-251). On `PUT freeze`, worksheet.controller.ts:122 calls `safeWorksheetRecordEntries(ws.merges ?? {})`, itself a full O(n) materialization of the CRDT record, before the function is entered. The added cost is two numeric-comparator sorts (~log n cheap compares per element) plus two shallow array copies — roughly a 2-3x factor on an already-mandatory walk, not an amplification that creates a stall the attacker did not already have. Under the ceiling the v1 API does enforce (MaxMergeEntries = 10000, checked pre-loop and post-loop at worksheet-settings.ts:127-133 and :178-181) the two sorts are ~130k comparisons, i.e. sub-millisecond.

(2) The premise it leans on is a separate pre-existing gap. An unbounded map seated via the CRDT path (client-side-only budget check at yorkie-store.ts:989) already stalls the loop through the pre-existing `parseRef`/`toSref` walk and through `rebuildMergeCoverMap` on load. This function neither creates nor materially widens that.

(3) Lane fit. CPU/availability amplification is not in this lens's enumerated lane (authz, secrets, injection, crypto/auth, SSRF, deserialization, path traversal). Even read generously as "unsafe input handling", the implied fix — sort once rather than twice, drop the `[...ranges]` copies — is a hardening nit, not a blocking security weakness. The reviewer concedes the same ("an amplification of an existing walk rather than a new class of exposure").
